conjecture.field_A: Mahler measure / heights of multivariate polynomials in algebraic number theory (Smyth's L'(χ_{-3},-1) closed form for m(1+s+t); Boyd–Deninger zeta-value formulae; Lehmer's problem). The logarithmic Mahler measure m(P) = ∫_{T^k} log|P| dμ is a classical height invariant essentially absent from the communication-complexity literature.
conjecture.field_B: Randomized two-party communication complexity R_{1/3}(f) of sign matrices M_f ∈ {-1,+1}^{2^n×2^n}, with DISJ_n as the canonical Ω(n) target (Razborov 1992) accessed through the discrepancy-style proxy R_{1/3}(f) ≥ (1/2) log_2(1/disc(M_f)) − O(1).
conjecture.statement: For f:{0,1}^n × {0,1}^n → {-1,+1} with sign matrix M_f, define the multilinear matrix polynomial F_f(s_1,...,s_n,t_1,...,t_n) = Σ_{x,y∈{0,1}^n} M_f(x,y) · ∏_{i=1}^n s_i^{x_i} t_i^{y_i} ∈ Z[s,t], and its 2n-torus logarithmic Mahler measure m(F_f) = ∫_{[0,1]^{2n}} log|F_f(e^{2πiθ_1},...,e^{2πiφ_n})| dθ dφ. Conjecture: (a) m(F_{DISJ_n}) − m(F_{const}) ≥ n · m(1+s+t) − o(n) = (0.32307...)·n − o(n), and (b) for every f, R_{1/3}(f) ≥ c · (m(F_f) − n·log 2) − O(log n) for an absolute c > 0. A single instance with R_{1/3} = O(log n) but m(F_f) − n·log 2 = ω(log n) refutes (b); an instance of DISJ with sublinear m refutes (a).
conjecture.rationale: The multilinear polynomial F_f is the natural Fourier-side / generating-function avatar of M_f under the {0,1}^n × {0,1}^n product structure; for DISJ the polynomial factors as 2∏(1+s_i+t_i) − ∏(1+s_i)(1+t_i), whose Mahler measure inherits Smyth's exact L-value per coordinate and gives a clean Ω(n) signature, while easy functions (constant, equality up to a row/column permutation, low-rank patterns) collapse F_f into a product of small-height factors with bounded m. Heights/Mahler measure are coordinate-respectful (multiplicative under tensor product, monotone under specialization), so they should track the multiplicative structure that makes DISJ hard, in a way orthogonal to spectral or discrepancy invariants.

conjecture.title: Lasserre Moment-Rank Gap of Accept Set Bounds AC0 PARITY Size
conjecture.field_A: Sum-of-squares / Lasserre hierarchy moment-matrix theory (Lasserre 2001, Parrilo 2003, Grigoriev 2001) — specifically the empirical degree-k pseudo-moment Gram matrix M_k(f) := (1/|f^{-1}(1)|) sum_{x in f^{-1}(1)} v_k(x) v_k(x)^T over the multilinear monomial vector v_k(x) of degree <= k on the boolean cube, used here as an S_n-equivariant non-uniform circuit invariant rather than as a CSP relaxation; its R-rank is poly-time via SVD and is essentially absent from the AC^0 / switching-lemma literature.
conjecture.field_B: AC^0 depth-d formula size for PARITY_n in the Hastad / Razborov-Smolensky lineage; the canonical NEXP-vs-AC^0 gateway target where tight size constants for d>=3 remain open.
conjecture.statement: For every boolean f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1} and integer k <= n/2, let rk_k(f) := rank_R(M_k(f)) <= N_k where N_k = sum_{j<=k} C(n,j). Conjecture (A): rk_k(PARITY_n) = N_k for every k <= floor(n/2) (full Lasserre rank of the even-parity accept set up to half-degree). Conjecture (B): for every AC^0 depth-d formula F of size s computing g on n variables, rk_k(g) <= s * k * C(n, k-1) for every 2 <= k <= n/2. Combining (A) and (B) at k = ceil(n^{1/(d-1)}) forces any AC^0 depth-d formula for PARITY_n to have size >= N_k / (k * C(n,k-1)) = 2^{Omega(n^{1/(d-1)} / log n)}; one counterexample to (A) at any (n,k <= n/2) or to (B) at any (F,k,g) refutes the conjecture.
conjecture.rationale: PARITY's accept set is the unique S_n-invariant antipodal half-cube and so should saturate every Lasserre moment-matrix dimension below half-degree, while AC^0 formulas of size s decompose their accept set as a union of s subcubes whose moment-matrix support sits inside an O(s)-dimensional (k*C(n,k-1))-spanned subspace of the multilinear monomial basis (one degree-(k-1) factor per gate fan-in). Re-expressing the Hastad/Razborov barrier as a moment-matrix rank deficit makes the lower bound a single linear-algebraic invariant computable in O((2^n + N_k) N_k^2) time. The bridge sits squarely in the SOS-hierarchy framework — Lasserre level-k rank for empirical pseudo-distributions on f^{-1}(1) — while being a non-uniform circuit lower bound rather than a CSP integrality gap, occupying a corner with <5 papers.
